assumptions: Assays for lipid peroxidation and membrane-permeability can be optimized for low-biomass, particle-enriched fractions (sensitivity and linearity must be established).
Lipid-oxidation events relevant for membrane protection will be detectable before complete loss of particle counts or large proteomic changes.
Spike-in controls or parallel positive-control EVs can be used to validate assay recovery and to flag assay interference by formulation excipients.
biological_rationale: Membrane integrity is central to the 'membrane-protected cargo' thesis used across the SGL-001 hypotheses. Chemical damage to phospholipids (peroxidation) or increased membrane permeability can abolish membrane-protection of cargo and mask surface epitopes without reducing bulk particle counts. Measuring lipid oxidation and membrane permeability directly provides orthogonal, chemistry-centered evidence that is mechanistically linked to the protection hypothesis and distinct from prior capture/protein/omic-focused proposals.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: BODIPY C11 ratiometric oxidation readout on capture-positive fractions; confirmatory oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS when material allows.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV membrane lipid peroxidation (qualitative flag)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Direct chemical readout of oxidized membrane lipids provides an orthogonal indicator that membranes have been chemically compromised, which should correspond with loss of membrane-protected cargo.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: assay sensitivity on low-biomass fractions must be established.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Membrane-impermeant dye uptake or luciferase-based leakage surrogate applied to captured intact EV eluates; qualitative threshold (presence of dye uptake above buffer/spike-in control) as fail.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV membrane permeability (dye-exclusion; qualitative pass/fail)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Increased membrane permeability (dye uptake) indicates loss of membrane integrity and would falsify the membrane-protected cargo hypothesis even when particle counts are unchanged.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: method adaptation required for small particle capture eluates; interference controls are essential.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed capture-signal loss could result from epitope masking (conformational) rather than chemical lipid damage; both may coexist.
edges.missing_experiment: Direct correlation of lipid-oxidation and membrane-permeability changes with capture-protection loss and protected-cargo loss across controlled exposures.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV emphasizes membrane protection as discriminating EVs; rodent work indicates process sensitivity but does not measure lipid peroxidation directly.

edges.competing_explanation: Even when membranes are chemically intact, delivery or species-specific clearance could limit in vivo detectability; lipid measures are necessary but not always sufficient as predictors.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo bridging using materials stratified by lipid-oxidation/permeability status to test predictive value for recoverable exposure and ex vivo readouts.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal biodistribution uncertainty makes early chemical flags particularly valuable to avoid wasted bridging studies.

nodes.statement: EV membrane lipid peroxidation and increased membrane permeability (measured chemically) reflect loss of membrane-protected cargo and are mechanistically upstream of loss of capture-protection signatures used to define EV identity and potency.

Storage/formulation/device/process exposures (temperature excursions, freeze-thaw, surfactant-containing excipients, high-shear) cause oxidative or physicochemical membrane damage that increases peroxidation and permeability while leaving bulk particle counts similar.

If lipid-oxidation and membrane-permeability changes are observed reproducibly after defined failure-condition exposures, these attributes can serve as early stability indicators that predict later loss of orthogonal capture/protection and protected-cargo signals and thus de-risk downstream bridging experiments.

competing_explanations: Loss of capture-protection readouts could be dominated by epitope masking or detergent-incompatible excipients rather than chemical lipid damage; buffer-compatibility controls are required.
Apparent peroxidation signals might originate from co-isolated soluble lipid-containing complexes rather than EV membranes if fractionation is incomplete.
dependencies: Validated capture/elution buffer compatibility for lipid and permeability assays
Analytical method development to demonstrate sensitivity on low-biomass fractions
At least 3 independent conditioned-medium lots for reproducibility
design_question: Which orthogonal, chemistry-focused attributes (EV membrane lipid peroxidation and membrane-permeability changes) reliably report loss of intact-EV membrane integrity and predict downstream loss of capture-protected signatures after clinically relevant storage and formulation exposures for intranasal MSC-conditioned-medium-derived materials?
expected_measurable_effect: Specific exposures that cause loss of orthogonal capture/protection signatures will also produce increased lipid peroxidation signal (e.g., increased BODIPY C11 oxidation ratio or TBARS readout) and increased membrane-permeability (dye uptake in a membrane-impermeant fluorescent probe assay) in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions, while particle counts remain similar.

experiment.assay: Tiered orthogonal assays on capture-positive particle-peak fractions: (1) BODIPY C11 ratiometric fluorescence to measure real-time lipid peroxidation; (2) TBARS colorimetric readout as orthogonal peroxidation check; (3) membrane-permeability dye uptake assay on intact-capture eluates; (4) confirmatory targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS on material-limited samples; (5) parallel particle counts (NTA/TRPS) and capture-protection ELISA/readout (detergent + protease) to correlate with chemistry endpoints.
experiment.comparator: Within-lot matched arms: (A) baseline handling (no exposure), (B) accelerated temperature exposure (e.g., 25°C for defined short term), (C) 3 freeze-thaw cycles, (D) incubation in formulation-buffer A (no surfactant) + device passage, (E) formulation-buffer B (low non-ionic surfactant) + high-shear device passage. Include detergent-disrupted positive controls and spike-in recovery controls.
experiment.control: Positive controls: characterized small EV prep subjected to detergent disruption (positive peroxidation/permeability signal) and spike-in tracer recovery per sample to confirm assay performance. Negative controls: buffer-only and untreated capture-eluted fractions.
dependencies: Assay development to establish LLOQ and specificity of BODIPY C11 and permeability dye assays for low-biomass fractions
Capture-elution buffer optimization to avoid assay interference
Availability of spike-in positive controls and sufficient fraction material for LC-MS confirmation
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible chemistry-centered signal differences (peroxidation or permeability) across tested failure-condition exposures despite validated spike-in recovery and observed loss of capture/protection signatures (i.e., chemistry readouts do not track with functional/identity loss), or chemistry signals are equally present in baseline and control arms (lack discrimination).
experiment.falsification_outcome: If lipid-oxidation and permeability readouts do not reproducibly differentiate exposed vs baseline capture-positive fractions (despite concurrent loss of capture/protection signatures), the hypothesis that these chemistry-centered measures are stability-indicating is falsified. The program should then deprioritize lipid chemistry attributes for gating and focus on alternative orthogonal identity/stability attributes (protected-cargo fingerprint, capture-compatibility matrices) or refine assay sensitivity.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Controlled storage/formulation/device exposures produce detectable increases in lipid-oxidation and membrane-permeability in capture-positive particle fractions that correlate with loss of orthogonal capture-protection signatures, enabling these chemistry-centered attributes to be used as stability indicators.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative increase in BODIPY C11 oxidation ratio and positive permeability dye uptake in exposed capture-positive fractions compared with baseline controls, with particle counts remaining within +/- 20% of baseline (qualitative similarity) and capture-protection readout showing concurrent loss in exposed arms.
experiment.question: Do clinically relevant storage and downstream exposures (accelerated temperature, 3 freeze-thaw cycles, representative excipient classes including low-level non-ionic surfactant, and device-simulated shear) produce reproducible increases in EV membrane lipid peroxidation and membrane permeability in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions while particle counts remain similar?
required_material: >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from same source-cell bank (matched passage) processed to yield capture-positive particle-peak fractions (bounded small-EV fraction) and concentrated conditioned-medium controls
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species/isotope-labeled) for per-sample recovery controls
BODIPY C11 reagent and fluorescence-capable plate reader or flow setup adapted for low-biomass fractions
TBARS chemistry reagents as orthogonal peroxidation check and LC-MS reagents for targeted oxidized-phospholipid confirmation when material allows
Membrane-permeability dye reagents adapted for nanoparticle capture eluates (e.g., Sytox variant or calcein-AM leakage surrogate) with validated buffer-compatibility
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Immuno-capture reagents for intact capture of canonical EV surface markers and capture-elution reagents (compatible with lipid assays)
Detergent (Triton X-100) and protease (proteinase K) for positive-disruption controls
Representative formulation excipient panels (matrix across pH, ionic strength, low non-ionic surfactant levels), freeze-thaw capability, and device-shear simulation rig
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: TBARS signal presence/absence in exposed vs baseline fractions
Targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS confirmation (presence of specific oxidized phosphatidylcholine species) where material allows
Spike-in recovery percentage to validate assay function
Protein:particle ratio per fraction to detect co-isolate changes
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent lots, at least one defined failure exposure (e.g., 3 freeze-thaw or formulation-buffer B + high-shear device passage) reproducibly produces (A) an increased BODIPY C11 oxidation ratio in capture-positive particle-peak fractions and (B) a positive membrane-permeability dye uptake signal, while particle counts remain similar and spike-in recovery confirms assay performance. Concurrent loss of capture-protection readout in the same arms strengthens the attribute's predictive value.

explicit_inferences: Direct chemistry-based measures of membrane damage provide an orthogonal, mechanistically relevant stability attribute distinct from protein/omic capture signatures.
A positive lipid-oxidation or membrane-permeability readout in capture-positive fractions should trigger process/formulation mitigation prior to in vivo bridging.
falsification_criteria: If materials subjected to clinically relevant failure exposures show no reproducible increase in lipid-oxidation or membrane-permeability in capture-positive fractions (while orthogonal capture/protection assays concurrently show loss), the hypothesis that chemistry-centered lipid measures are stability-indicating is falsified.

If lipid-oxidation/permeability signals are ubiquitous across both bounded small-EV fractions and secretome-retaining controls (no discrimination), the attributes lack discriminative value and are falsified for gating purposes.
human_decisions_required: Select specific BODIPY C11 assay format and confirm instrumentation availability and sensitivity
Define qualitative pass/fail thresholds for peroxidation and permeability readouts (after assay development) before execution
Approve candidate failure-condition matrix (temperatures, freeze-thaw cycles, excipient/device envelopes) to test
manufacturability_assessment: Lipid-oxidation assays (e.g., BODIPY C11 fluorescence shift, targeted oxidized phospholipid LC-MS) and membrane-permeability dye-exclusion assays can be performed on capture-positive, particle-peak fractions at pilot scale. Assay development and sensitivity qualification are required; reagents and methods are standard in analytical labs and amenable to transfer.
manufacturing_rationale: Lipid peroxidation and membrane permeability assays are amenable to fit-for-purpose qualification, can be applied to low-biomass capture-positive fractions, and are potentially more transferable across sites and platforms than some proteomic signatures. They can be incorporated into stability matrix testing (temperatures, freeze-thaw, excipient/device exposures) to flag conditions that chemically damage particle membranes before investing in complex multi-omic or in vivo bridging work.
measurement_strategy: Apply a two-tier orthogonal chemistry strategy on fraction-level material: (A) colorimetric/fluorescent peroxidation reporter (BODIPY C11 ratiometric assay) and TBARS as orthogonal corroboration; (B) membrane-permeability dye-exclusion (e.g., Sytox-based or calcein-AM leakage surrogate adapted to captured particles) measured on intact-capture eluates; (C) targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS on the same capture-positive fractions to confirm chemical identity for high-confidence failures. Spike-in characterized EV controls and buffer-compatibility checks run in parallel.
novelty_statement: This proposal departs materially from prior SGL-001 stability proposals by focusing on direct chemical measures of membrane integrity (lipid peroxidation and membrane permeability) rather than expanding capture/protection, proteomic, or multi-omic fingerprints. The experiment tests chemistry-centered, mechanism-linked stability attributes that can provide earlier, orthogonal flags of membrane damage and thereby reduce wasted downstream bridging studies.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity: peroxidation and permeability assays may lack sensitivity on low-biomass fractions.
Assay interference: formulation excipients or capture/elution buffers may interfere with fluorescent reporters; buffer-compatibility controls are required.
Over-reliance: chemical flags may be necessary but not sufficient predictors of in vivo delivery failures driven by administration/species factors.
proposed_potency_relationship: These attributes are intended as stability indicators rather than direct potency measures. However, loss of membrane integrity (peroxidation/permeability) is expected to precede and predict loss of membrane-protected bioactivity and capture-protection signatures; therefore they will gate whether potency linkage experiments proceed.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt EV membrane lipid-oxidation and membrane-permeability (dye-exclusion) readouts, measured on particle-peak / capture-positive fractions, as complementary stability-indicating attributes alongside orthogonal capture/protection assays — use a qualitative pass/fail decision rule (evidence of increased lipid oxidation or increased membrane permeability = fail) to flag compromised lots for follow-up potency and identity linkage.
title: Stability hypothesis: Lipid-oxidation and membrane-permeability assays as orthogonal stability-indicating attributes for SGL-001
